mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be negative due to persistent discount rate expectations and reduced liquidity in the equity market.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5.0 and no change in FEDFUNDS for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger is active.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a single month is associated with a short-term positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as investors anticipate future rate cuts and demand for risk assets increases.
failure_condition: Across 20 triggered events, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs in two consecutive months coincides with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as labor market strength supports optimism about corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly > 200,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In regimes matching the trigger, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) contraction of more than 2% while employment (PAYEMS) remains above 150,000 is associated with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to recessionary demand destruction.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -2.0 and PAYEMS monthly > 150,000
failure_condition: During 10 such triggered events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in home sales (HOUST) of more than 10% signals weakening demand, which predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate slower corporate revenue growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change < -10.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 5 such triggers, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 3.5% (UNRATE < 3.5%) for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be positive due to increased consumer and business confidence.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE monthly < 3.5 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 8 such regimes, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the mean of non-trigger periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the monthly real GDP deflator (CPIAUCSL) growth rate above 0.3% for four consecutive months, in the context of rising FEDFUNDS, predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to inflation concerns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3 for four consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS monthly > 4.0
failure_condition: During 6 such triggers, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) below 500 million dollars in a single month, coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO), predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as a recessionary supply shock unfolds.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly < 500.0 and INDPRO monthly < 105.0 for the same month
failure_condition: Across 7 such triggered events, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (one-tailed t-test p > 0.05).
